info.title: VolleyStat Local Development API
info.description: LOCAL TEST DATA ONLY. Every route except health, register and login needs a session. No trained AI. Never expose to the internet.

put.description:
Create the match under an id the client chose, or return the match that already has it.

A client that picks the id before its first request can address the match whatever happens
to the answer: it repeats this call, or deletes the match, with the id it already holds.
With POST the id exists only in the answer, and a lost answer leaves a match nobody can
delete. A repeat never changes what the first request stored, and only an account that may
read the match gets it back; any other account gets 403 NOT_A_MEMBER.

201.description: The match was created under this id

delete.description:
Remove a match and everything the server holds for it: its record, uploads, videos, analyses and bytes.

Deleting a video leaves the match record and the upload rows behind. This is the call a
client makes when the user removes the match itself, so that nothing of it stays. A match
that belongs to no account (LEGACY) answers 403; the operator deletes it (`legacy --delete`).

put.description:
Set the rule the server counts the sets of this match with.

A rule that differs from the stored one moves the rally list of every analysis of the match
that has rallies one version on, in the same transaction. The user confirmed those lists
while looking at set scores of the old rule, so each confirmation lapses, and a confirmation
or a correction still on its way with the old version is refused as stale. Answers, cards and
corrections stay as they are.

The rule the match already has changes nothing, so a repeated request lands once. Any other
request must name the rule the match has now (expectedRules). A request that names another rule
was sent before a later change, and it is refused as stale instead of undoing that change.
Only the rules are compared: a late request lands when the match is back at the rule it names.

post.description:
Start an upload of a video of the match. The quotas, the server-wide pool and the free-disk
floor are checked in the transaction that inserts the row (docs/API_V1.md, section 10).

A start the account repeats for the same file (same match, checksum, size, name and type) gets
the unfinished upload it already has, before any limit is checked: a phone that lost the first
answer never learned that upload's id, and a second row would hold the same bytes twice.

200.description: This account already had an unfinished upload of the same file for this match; the answer names it and the offset to continue from

delete.description: Give up an unfinished upload and free its bytes.

post.description: Run the file check again for a video that could not be validated earlier.

get.description:
Evidence playback: the client plays the clip of a review card from these bytes.

The player sends the session in the Authorization header too; no address carries a token.

post.description: Add a rally that the analyzer missed.
Set the start and the end of a rally. A changed end asks for the winner again.
Cut a rally that holds two. The later part is the rally whose end the user may already have judged.
Join a rally with the one before it. The earlier one was no rally of its own, so its answers go.
Record that the user declares the list complete: it holds every rally of the video.
Open an account. The gate comes first, so nothing about the username leaks while it is closed.
Open a session. A wrong password and an unknown username get the same answer and cost the same.

get.description: The caller's account and teams. The teams are the list GET /v1/teams answers.

put.description: Set a new password. Every other session of the account ends and every phone is forgotten.

post.description:
Delete the account with its personal matches: their uploads, videos, analyses and bytes,
then the user row, its sessions, its phones, its memberships and its blocks. Nothing of it stays in
the file.

Every team the account captains passes to its earliest-joined other member, or goes when nobody else
is in it. Matches that belong to no account (LEGACY) stay; the operator deletes them.

get.description: The teams of the caller, in the order the caller joined them.

put.description:
Create a team under an id the client chose, or return the caller's team that already has it.

The server draws the tag, creates the team's seat pool (6 starter seats and the substitute seats) and makes
the caller its captain on the seat the body names. A repeat by a member answers 200 and changes nothing;
another account gets 409 TEAM_ID_TAKEN. A refused body writes nothing and takes no place of the day.

201.description: The team was created under this id

get.description: The team as a member sees it.

delete.description: Delete the team with its seat pool, memberships and blocks (captain). Nothing of it stays in the file.

put.description: Set the team's name and usual match day and time (captain). A null schedule clears it.

Set the substitute count and move members between starter and substitute seats (captain).

The server checks the final state: the same body twice changes nothing. The 6 starter seats never change.

Set or clear a member's jersey: a member's own, or anyone's by the captain. A jersey is unique among the
members of one team.

delete.description:
Leave the team (the caller's own id) or remove a member (captain).

A removal blocks the removed account in the team's pool in the same transaction; leaving writes no block.
Either frees the member's seat with its type. A captain with other members hands the captaincy on first
(409 CAPTAIN_MUST_TRANSFER); a captain alone deletes the team by leaving.

get.description: The accounts the captain removed from the team, in the order of their removal (captain).

delete.description: Lift the block of a removed account (captain). A block that does not exist answers the same.

post.description:
Move the captain's mark for the new-member badge to `upTo` (captain).

The mark never moves back, and never past the server's time, so a member who joins later still counts as
new.

Hand the captaincy to another member (captain), who may captain at most CAPTAIN_LIMIT teams with it.

Both role changes happen in one transaction and the seats stay. The answer is the team as the caller now
sees it. A transfer to the caller changes nothing.

put.description:
Set both images of the team's logo (captain).

Each image is a simple lossy WebP: at most 256 px and 36 KiB for members, at most 128 px and 8 KiB for link
views. The first image that breaks the rule is named in 422 LOGO_INVALID, and nothing is written. A change
moves the logo's version; the same bytes again change nothing. A replaced logo leaves no bytes behind: the
rows are overwritten with zeros (secure_delete) and the write-ahead log is emptied after the commit.

delete.description: Remove both images of the team's logo (captain) and move its version. Without a logo nothing changes.

get.description: One image of the team's logo (member). The ETag is the logo's version, so a phone that holds it gets 304.

304.description: If-None-Match names the logo's current version

JoinsSeenInput.title: JoinsSeenInput
JoinsSeenInput.description: The moment up to which the captain has seen the members who joined, as the team screen showed them.

LinkReference.title: LinkReference
LinkReference.description: A share link by its token or by its code: exactly one of the two.

LogoInput.title: LogoInput
LogoInput.description: Both images of a logo in base64: at most 256 px for members and at most 128 px for link views (design 4.2).

MatchRulesChange.title: MatchRulesChange
MatchRulesChange.description:
A rule change. It also names the rule its sender last read. While the match has another rule,
a request the phone gave up on is refused, so it does not undo a later change to another rule.
The check compares rules: when later changes brought the match back to the rule the request
names, the late request still lands (ADR-0115).

MatchRulesInput.title: MatchRulesInput
MatchRulesInput.description: The rule the user chose: the app offers exactly these values, so the server accepts nothing else.

Schedule.title: Schedule
Schedule.description: The team's usual match day and time: 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday, and HH:MM.

SeatsInput.title: SeatsInput
SeatsInput.description: The final state the captain wants: the substitute count and the members who change their seat type.

HTTPBearer.description: The session token from register or login
